text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to melt.

Gerald, an avid collector of invisible art, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind’ at an auction. He bid against himself and won, celebrating by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table, because the food, of course, was too shy to show up. The candles on the table were made entirely of silence, burning with a flame that emitted no light but rather a profound sense of disappointment. Gerald lit them with a match made of pure logic, which immediately exploded because it couldn't handle the absurdity of the situation. The guests, who were all reflections in a mirror that had decided to quit its job, sat down to eat the silence, finding it surprisingly crunchy and lacking in nutritional value. Gerald raised a glass of water that was actually just a hole in the air, toasted to his own reflection, and then vanished, leaving behind only the smell of Tuesday and a single, unlit candle that was waiting for permission to exist.
